inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement: share-based compensation $71.753m plus 'stock repurchased for payroll taxes and other' $25.115m (financing). No combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published, so the two lines are summed. Interest income ($4.2m FY2025) is NOT stripped: JBHT is a net-debt company with $4m of cash, so there is no cash pile to double-count.
inputs.share_count_basis: 93.915m actual shares outstanding at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2-26 press release) plus ~0.8m dilutive RSU/PSU (Q2-26 diluted 94.944m vs basic 94.125m weighted) = 94.7m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC incl. net-settlement taxes is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks ($923m FY2025, $178m H1-2026) are the cash mechanism funding the flat count and are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30-Jun-2026 10-Q: $750m 4.90% senior notes due Mar-2030 + $350m term loans + $54m revolver (carrying $1,145.3m, avg rate 4.61% on the facility) less $4.2m cash. The $700m notes maturing Mar-2026 were repaid at par in the half. Operating lease liabilities ($253.7m PV at FY2025; $106.8m cash paid in 2025) are EXCLUDED: US GAAP charges operating leases inside operating expense, so the lease cost is already in EBITDA (treatment B).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~4.1% + beta ~1.1 x ERP ~4.8% = ~9.4% cost of equity; ~5% debt weight at 4.9% pre-tax / ~3.7% after-tax; blended ~9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios -- freight-cycle risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- operating leases are an operating cost under US GAAP (noncash lease expense $96m inside opex); lease liabilities excluded from net debt; no separate lease_cost_pct_path needed.
inputs.capex_basis: Projection capex_pct is on JBHT's own NET capital expenditure definition (additions less proceeds from equipment sales/trade-ins), which is how management guides ($600-800m for CY2026). reported_fcf and last_fcf are on the Metrics CSV's GROSS-capex basis (OCF $1,678m less additions $731m); on the net basis FY2025 FCF would be $1,103m. Both are above mid-cycle: FY2025 cash taxes were only ~14% of EBIT (bonus depreciation) and OCF carried ~$365m of non-earnings inflows (deferred tax, working capital).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). JBHT is an asset-based intermodal (JBI ~50% of revenue), dedicated (DCS ~26%), brokerage (ICS), final-mile (FMS) and truckload (JBT) operator; no bank/REIT/holdco features. MID-CYCLE: the 2023-25 freight recession took operating margin from 9.0% (FY2022 peak) to 6.9% (FY2024 trough); FY2025 7.2%, Q2-2026 7.4% with intermodal volume +10% and revenue +19% (+11% ex-fuel). EBITDA margin has been remarkably stable at 13.2-13.5% through the cycle because D&A absorbed the 2022-23 container/chassis build (net capex $1.4-1.6bn/yr) -- the cyclicality shows up in EBIT and in capex, not in EBITDA. The base path therefore holds EBITDA at ~13.6% (EBIT ~8%, between FY2019's 8.0% and the FY2022 peak), lets net capex normalise UP from the current post-overbuild holiday (4.8% of revenue FY2025; guided ~5% CY2026) to a ~6.7% through-cycle level that funds D&A (~5.5%) plus fleet growth, and ramps cash tax from ~20% (bonus depreciation, permanent under the 2025 Act) toward the guided 24-24.5% GAAP rate. Year-1 owner FCF (~$680m) sits below the FY2025 actual ($851m gross-capex basis) by design: it removes the FY2025 cash-tax and working-capital windfalls. No Analysis.json existed at build time; business judgments come from the FY2025 10-K, Q2-2026 10-Q and Q2-2026 press release (EDGAR).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025); equity CAGR is distorted by $2.0bn of buybacks over the period and owner-FCF CAGRs measure a capex trough against the FY2022-23 build, so neither is a usable anchor. 10-year revenue CAGR FY2015-25 is 6.8%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (6.5%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (4.5%) and 3yr CAGRs are all negative (FY2022 peak base). Equity is flattered by retained earnings on a shrinking share count; revenue CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less net-settlement taxes, gross-capex basis): FY2020 $324m, FY2021 $215m, FY2022 $159m, FY2023 -$234m, FY2024 $516m, FY2025 $851m. The 3yr/5yr owner-FCF CAGRs (75%/21%) are trough-to-peak capex-cycle noise, not a growth trend; FY2025 is a capex-holiday and cash-tax-deferral year and is not repeatable as a base.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +11.5%: H1-26 was +12.0% reported (+19% in Q2, of which ~8pp fuel surcharge); H2 comps are similar so ~$13.4bn for the year. Fuel surcharge revenue is near-zero-margin, hence the FY2026 EBITDA margin dip to 12.8%. FY2027-28 +5-5.5% as the intermodal upcycle continues ex-fuel; then decays to the 2.5% terminal rate, in line with the 4.5% 5yr / 6.8% 10yr revenue CAGRs.
base.capex_rationale: Net capex 5.2% of revenue in FY2026 (~$700m, midpoint of the $600-800m guide), then normalising to ~6.7-6.8%: D&A ~5.6% plus ~1pp of fleet-growth capex (net PP&E is ~45% of revenue, so 2.5-3% growth needs ~1.2pp). The 2022-23 container overbuild is what makes the current holiday temporary.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables (~10.5% of revenue) exceed payables and accruals (~8%): growth consumes ~3-4% of the revenue increase. H1-26 receivables absorbed $301m on a $700m half-year revenue increase, fuel-inflated; -4% of the change is used.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 freight upturn is real but partly fuel: revenue ex-fuel grows high single digits in 2026 and mid single digits in 2027-28 as intermodal keeps converting highway freight (Eastern network +16% loads in Q2-26) and DCS grows trucks at ~96% retention. Operating margin recovers to ~8% (EBITDA ~13.6%, D&A ~5.6%) -- between FY2019 and the FY2022 peak -- as structural-cost programs and dray/container-utilisation gains offset insurance and driver inflation. ICS and JBT stay marginal contributors. Net capex normalises from the post-overbuild holiday to ~6.7% of revenue; cash tax ramps to the guided 24%. Owner FCF is roughly flat at $650-800m for the decade because rising capex offsets margin recovery -- the asset-heavy model converts ~55-65% of net income to owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: A multi-year intermodal cycle: sustained highway-to-rail conversion on fuel and driver scarcity, rail service holding, and the idle container/chassis capacity bought in 2022-23 filling without new growth capex. Operating margin returns to and holds the FY2022 peak (~9.4%; EBITDA 14.8%) as JBI network density and lower empty moves compound, DCS keeps pricing on indexed escalators, and ICS reaches sustainable profitability. Revenue compounds ~6% through 2030. Terminal growth 3% but the 15x owner-FCF cap binds, so the bull is a margin story, not a multiple story.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027 relapse: tariff/trade-policy shocks cut import-driven intermodal volumes, truckload capacity returns and collapses spot and contract rates (ICS gross margin already fell to 12.5% from 15.5%), rail service or BNSF contract terms deteriorate, and FMS keeps shedding accounts. Operating margin stalls at the FY2024 trough (~6.9%; EBITDA 12.6%) with insurance-claims and equipment inflation unrecovered; revenue is flat-to-low-single-digit for three years then grows at 2-2.5%. No solvency issue -- net debt is ~0.7x EBITDA and the revolver is undrawn to $946m -- so the bear is an earnings-power case, not a balance-sheet one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because JBHT is a freight cyclical one cycle out from a 30% margin compression, ICS/JBT are still loss-making-to-break-even, and Q2-26's headline growth was one-third fuel surcharge; not higher because the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk (0.7x net debt/EBITDA, notes due 2030). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things -- peak margins sustained for a decade, the intermodal cycle persisting, and ICS profitability -- the first of which JBHT achieved only in FY2022.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: SBC (incl. net-settlement taxes) fully expensed, flat diluted share count, net capex on the company's own definition normalised to a through-cycle level, cash taxes ramped to the guided GAAP rate, one 9% USD WACC across scenarios with cyclicality carried in the flows and weights. The valuation deliberately does not carry FY2025's capex holiday, bonus-depreciation cash-tax rate or working-capital release forward. JBHT is a high-quality, well-capitalised operator whose asset intensity caps owner-FCF conversion at roughly 55-65% of net income; the market prices it on P/E (~30x trailing) and a margin-recovery narrative, so a cash-flow model at a 9% discount rate lands well below the quote. The gap is the finding.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex normalisation is the single biggest driver: every 1pp of revenue in net capex (~$150m/yr) is worth roughly $20/share; if the 2022-23 container fleet absorbs growth for longer than modelled, value is higher.
Fuel surcharge inflation in 2026 revenue (~8pp in Q2) makes margin-% comparisons noisy; the FY2026 EBITDA margin dip is a denominator effect, not deterioration.
Cash tax: permanent 100% bonus depreciation could keep cash taxes ~4-5pp below the GAAP rate while capex grows -- an upside to the 24% terminal path.
Intermodal depends on BNSF (West) and CSX/NS (East) service and contract terms; a rail-service failure or contract reset is the sharpest single downside axis.
Insurance-claims and driver-wage inflation have run ahead of pricing since 2022 and are the margin ceiling in the base case.
